cond_0001.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the [Company name masked] Lab in the Departments of Neuroscience and Genetics.
The lab is broadly interested in neuroimmunology with a focus on microglial biology; additional areas of expertise include microglia, neurodegeneration, and single-cell genomics. The lab combines cutting-edge single-cell genomic technologies with in vitro and in vivo genetic, molecular, and cellular tools to investigate microglial development, heterogeneity, and mechanisms of neuro-immune interactions underlying brain structure and disease. This NIH-funded project is based on recent publications (Li et al. Neuron. 2019; Barclay et al. Biorxiv. 2024), Where the postdoc candidate will use novel tools and technologies (e.g. Single-cell multi-omics, viral manipulation, CRISPR) to study microglial plasticity and gene regulation in neurodegeneration diseases.
The postdoctoral researcher will have the opportunity to work with collaborators inside and outside the University, and develop the skills to become an independent scientist.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Manages their own project, which should lead to a first author publication.
Develops expertise in cutting-edge technologies.
Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, public speaking, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Develops mentorship skills by training junior students and staff.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University with excellent oral communication skills.
Assists with grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers on research with excellent writing skills.
Designs research experiments.
Evaluates research findings and reports results.
Conscientious discharge of research responsibilities.
Maintains conformity with ethical standards in research.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
Engages in open and timely discussion with their mentor regarding possession, distribution of material, reagents, records belonging to their laboratory and any proposed disclosure of findings, techniques privately or in publications.
Collegial conduct towards co-trainees, staff members and members of the research group.
Adherence to all applicable University policies, procedures and regulations. All data, research records, research materials and other intellectual property generated in University laboratories remain the property of the University.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Ph.D. Degree in biology, biomedical sciences, or a related field.
Preferred Requirements
Prior experience in molecular neuroscience, glial biology, and/or neurodegeneration.
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0001.values: We value work that supports people well and reflects genuine care in how it is done. We believe responsibility and respect matter as much as the end result.
cond_0001.inclusion: [Company name masked] is an equal opportunities employer. We believe passionately that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We make recruiting decisions based on your experience and skills. We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build.

cond_0270.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the [Company name masked] Lab in the Departments of Neuroscience and Genetics.
The lab works broadly in neuroimmunology with a focus on microglial biology, neurodegeneration, and single-cell genomics. The work combines cutting-edge single-cell genomic technologies with in vitro and in vivo genetic, molecular, and cellular tools to investigate microglial development, heterogeneity, and mechanisms of neuro-immune interactions underlying brain structure and disease. This NIH-funded project builds on recent publications (Li et al. Neuron. 2019; Barclay et al. Biorxiv. 2024), Where the postdoc candidate will work with novel tools and technologies (e.g. Single-cell multi-omics, viral manipulation, CRISPR) to study microglial plasticity and gene regulation in neurodegeneration diseases.
The postdoctoral researcher will have the opportunity to collaborate with partners inside and outside the University, and develop the skills to become an independent scientist.
cond_0270.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Coordinates with the mentor and team to advance their own project, which should lead to a first author publication.
Develops expertise in cutting-edge technologies.
Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, public speaking, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Supports junior students and staff by sharing mentorship and training.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University with excellent oral communication skills.
Assists with grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers on research with excellent writing skills.
Collaborates on the design of research experiments.
Evaluates research findings and shares results with the group.
Conscientious discharge of research responsibilities.
Maintains conformity with ethical standards in research.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
Engages in open and timely discussion with their mentor regarding possession, distribution of material, reagents, records belonging to their laboratory and any proposed disclosure of findings, techniques privately or in publications.
Collegial conduct towards co-trainees, staff members and members of the research group.
Adherence to all applicable University policies, procedures and regulations. All data, research records, research materials and other intellectual property generated in University laboratories remain the property of the University.
cond_0270.requirements:
Ph.D. Degree in biology, biomedical sciences or a related field.
Prior experiences in molecular neuroscience, glial biology, and/or neurodegeneration are highly encouraged.

cond_0280.intro:
The [Company name masked] Lab is broadly interested in neuroimmunology with a focus on microglial biology; additional area of expertise in microglia, neurodegeneration, single cell genomics. Particularly, the lab is interested in combining cutting-edge single-cell genomic technologies with in vitro and in vivo genetic, molecular and cellular tools to investigate microglial development, heterogeneity and mechanisms of neuro-immune interactions underlying brain structure and disease. This NIH-funded project is based on recent publications (Li et al. Neuron. 2019; Barclay et al. Biorxiv. 2024), Where the postdoc candidate will use novel tools and technologies (e.g single-cell multi-omics, viral manipulation, CRISPR), to study microglial plasticity and gene regulation in neurodegeneration diseases.
The postdoctoral researcher will have the opportunity to work with collaborators inside and outside the University, and develop the skills to become an independent scientist.

cond_0324.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the [Company name masked] Lab in the Departments of Neuroscience and Genetics.
The lab works broadly in neuroimmunology with a focus on microglial biology, neurodegeneration, and single-cell genomics. The work combines cutting-edge single-cell genomic technologies with in vitro and in vivo genetic, molecular, and cellular tools to investigate microglial development, heterogeneity, and mechanisms of neuro-immune interactions underlying brain structure and disease. This NIH-funded project builds on recent publications (Li et al. Neuron. 2019; Barclay et al. Biorxiv. 2024), Where the postdoc candidate will work with novel tools and technologies (e.g. Single-cell multi-omics, viral manipulation, CRISPR) to study microglial plasticity and gene regulation in neurodegeneration diseases.
The postdoctoral researcher will have the opportunity to collaborate with partners inside and outside the University, and develop the skills to become an independent scientist.
cond_0324.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Coordinates with the mentor and team to advance their own project, which should lead to a first author publication.
Develops expertise in cutting-edge technologies.
Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, public speaking, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Supports junior students and staff by sharing mentorship and training.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University with excellent oral communication skills.
Assists with grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers on research with excellent writing skills.
Collaborates on the design of research experiments.
Evaluates research findings and shares results with the group.
Conscientious discharge of research responsibilities.
Maintains conformity with ethical standards in research.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
Engages in open and timely discussion with their mentor regarding possession, distribution of material, reagents, records belonging to their laboratory and any proposed disclosure of findings, techniques privately or in publications.
Collegial conduct towards co-trainees, staff members and members of the research group.
Adherence to all applicable University policies, procedures and regulations. All data, research records, research materials and other intellectual property generated in University laboratories remain the property of the University.
cond_0324.requirements:
Ph.D. Degree in biology, biomedical sciences or a related field.
Prior experiences in molecular neuroscience, glial biology, and/or neurodegeneration are highly encouraged.
Working Conditions: This position works in a laboratory environment with potential exposure to biological and chemical hazards. The individual must be physically able to wear protective equipment and to provide standard care to research animals.
Pre-Employment Screening: All external candidates receiving an offer for employment will be required to submit to pre-employment screening for this position. The screenings will include criminal background check and, as applicable for the position, other background checks, drug screen, an employment and education or licensure/certification verification, physical examination, certain vaccinations and/or governmental registry checks. All offers are contingent upon successful completion of required screening.

Particularly, the lab is interested in combining cutting-edge single-cell genomic technologies with in vitro and in vivo genetic, molecular and cellular tools to investigate microglial development, heterogeneity and mechanisms of neuro-immune interactions underlying brain structure and disease. This NIH-funded project is based on recent publications (Li et al. Neuron. 2019; Barclay et al. Biorxiv. 2024), Where the postdoc candidate will use novel tools and technologies (e.g single-cell multi-omics, viral manipulation, CRISPR), to study microglial plasticity and gene regulation in neurodegeneration diseases.
The postdoctoral researcher will have the opportunity to work with collaborators inside and outside the University, and develop the skills to become an independent scientist. People usually grow into this kind of research over time as they build hands-on experience with the tools and questions involved.
cond_0500.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Manages their own project, which should lead to a first author publication.
Develops expertise in cutting-edge technologies.
Develops proficiency in career skills, including writing, public speaking, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Develops mentorship skills by training junior students and staff.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University with excellent oral communication skills.
Assists with grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers on research with excellent writing skills.
Designs research experiments.
Evaluates research findings and reports results.
Conscientious discharge of research responsibilities.
Maintains conformity with ethical standards in research.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
Engages in open and timely discussion with their mentor regarding possession, distribution of material, reagents, records belonging to their laboratory and any proposed disclosure of findings, techniques privately or in publications.
Collegial conduct towards co-trainees, staff members and members of the research group.
Adherence to all applicable University policies, procedures and regulations. All data, research records, research materials and other intellectual property generated in University laboratories remain the property of the University.
cond_0500.requirements:
Ph.D. Degree in biology, biomedical sciences or a related field.
Prior experiences in molecular neuroscience, glial biology, and/or neurodegeneration are highly encouraged.

cond_0502.intro:
A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is open in the [Company name masked] Lab in the Departments of Neuroscience and Genetics.
The lab focuses on neuroimmunology with an emphasis on microglial biology, neurodegeneration, and single-cell genomics. The work involves combining single-cell genomic technologies with in vitro and in vivo genetic, molecular, and cellular tools to investigate microglial development, heterogeneity, and neuro-immune interactions underlying brain structure and disease. The postdoctoral researcher will have the opportunity to coordinate with collaborators inside and outside the University, and develop the skills to become an independent scientist.

The [Company name masked] Lab focuses on neuroimmunology with an emphasis on microglial biology, neurodegeneration, and single-cell genomics. The lab combines cutting-edge single-cell genomic technologies with in vitro and in vivo genetic, molecular, and cellular tools to investigate microglial development, heterogeneity, and mechanisms of neuro-immune interactions underlying brain structure and disease. This NIH-funded project builds on recent publications (Li et al. Neuron. 2019; Barclay et al. Biorxiv. 2024), Where the postdoc candidate will apply novel tools and technologies (e.g. Single-cell multi-omics, viral manipulation, CRISPR) to study microglial plasticity and gene regulation in neurodegeneration diseases.
The postdoctoral researcher will lead collaborations inside and outside the University and build the skills to become an independent scientist.
cond_0593.responsibilities:
Trains under the supervision of a faculty mentor including (but not limited to):
Owns and drives their own project, leading to a first author publication.
Develops expertise in cutting-edge technologies.
Builds proficiency in career skills, including writing, public speaking, networking, and critical evaluation of scientific literature.
Develops mentorship skills by training junior students and staff.
Presents scientific work both inside and outside the University with excellent oral communication skills.
Leads contributions to grant preparation and reporting.
Prepares and submits papers on research with excellent writing skills.
Designs research experiments.
Evaluates research findings and reports results.
Conscientious discharge of research responsibilities.
Maintains conformity with ethical standards in research.
Maintains compliance with good laboratory practice including the maintenance of adequate research records.
Engages in open and timely discussion with their mentor regarding possession, distribution of material, reagents, records belonging to their laboratory and any proposed disclosure of findings, techniques privately or in publications.
Collegial conduct towards co-trainees, staff members and members of the research group.
Adherence to all applicable University policies, procedures and regulations. All data, research records, research materials and other intellectual property generated in University laboratories remain the property of the University.
cond_0593.requirements:
Ph.D. Degree in biology, biomedical sciences or a related field.
Prior experiences in molecular neuroscience, glial biology, and/or neurodegeneration are highly encouraged.
Working Conditions: This position works in a laboratory environment with potential exposure to biological and chemical hazards. The individual must be physically able to wear protective equipment and to provide standard care to research animals.
